title: Windshield Frame Bracket Redesign and Sealant Standard Change — Issue 1

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: First issue of the windshield frame work, replacing the corner bracket and changing the sealant standard after moisture ingress at the lower forward corner was found to be the common factor in early windshield removals.

sections.reason: Windshield removals in the first four years of service ran at three times the predicted rate, and teardown showed moisture behind the seal at the lower forward corner on nineteen of twenty-four units examined. The bracket as delivered creates a shallow pocket at that corner where water collects during rain and washing, and the sealant originally specified loses adhesion at the pocket edge after repeated thermal cycling.
sections.description: The corner bracket is replaced by a variant with a drained profile that removes the pocket, and the frame interface is resealed to a revised standard with a higher temperature capability and a defined bead profile. The spar cap at the lower forward corner, which is obsolete and no longer supported, is replaced at the same time by the current item. The windshield pane itself and the heating film connections are unchanged; this modification is entirely in the surrounding frame and its sealing. The installation drawing is reissued with the new bead profile and the drain path.
sections.effects: Mass increase of one point nine kilograms per side. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable at bracket level. The windshield removal and installation tasks change for the sealing sequence and cure time, adding about ninety minutes to an installation. The flight crew limitation entry for windshield heating is unaffected in substance but is re-issued because it quotes the frame standard. Structure repair manual limits for the frame are unchanged.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00329. Retrofit is by bulletin at the next windshield change, so that the sealing work is done with the pane already out; a separate inspection bulletin identifies aircraft with existing corner corrosion.

type_data.production_impact: Cut in at MSN M00329, sealing standard aligned with the cockpit assembly station
